concept: Graph Indexing and Adjacency Traversal Engines
summary: Internal memory and storage layouts including CSR/CSC matrices, chunked adjacency lists, pointer swizzling, and vector-graph hybrid indexes.

facts.text: Compressed Sparse Row (CSR) and Compressed Sparse Column (CSC) formats provide static contiguous memory layouts with O(1) neighbor lookups and optimal cache-locality for analytical traversals, but require O(V+E) rebuilding overhead on dynamic graph updates.

Dynamic graph engines utilize chunked adjacency lists, differential updates, or LSM-tree-backed key-value stores (e.g. RocksDB in Memgraph and NebulaGraph) to balance write amplification with neighbor iteration throughput.

Vector-graph hybrid indexes integrate vector quantization (e.g. HNSW, IVF-PQ) into graph node storage, allowing simultaneous euclidean/cosine vector similarity filtering and topological neighbor expansion in a single scan.
